name: Butamirate

overview.mechanism: A cough suppressant evaluated in clinical and cough-challenge studies; these studies assess antitussive responses rather than validating a molecular mechanism [[BUTA-CHALLENGE,BUTA-CLIN]].
uses: Symptomatic cough suppression has been studied; verify locally approved indications and age/formulation restrictions [[BUTA-CLIN]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, six-way crossover; 59 healthy volunteers randomized.
rows.intervention: Four butamirate regimens, dextromethorphan and placebo; capsaicin cough challenges.
rows.findings: Dextromethorphan significantly attenuated challenge cough versus placebo; butamirate did not demonstrate significant activity.
rows.limitations: Experimental cough sensitivity in healthy adults is not patient-reported cough relief. This study does not establish clinical efficacy or a renal regimen.

rows.design: Double-blind randomized active-comparator trial; 60 patients, five days.
rows.intervention: Butamirate versus clobutinol for irritative or chronic cough.
rows.findings: Both groups improved; no significant overall between-group efficacy difference. A favorable carcinoma-cough subgroup finding involved only 14 patients.
rows.limitations: No placebo group, short follow-up and heterogeneous cough causes. The small subgroup does not establish a cancer-specific prescribing indication.

sources.citation: A randomized placebo controlled trial to evaluate the effects of butamirate and dextromethorphan on capsaicin induced cough in healthy volunteers. PubMed PMID: 24995954.
Comparative evaluation of the antitussive activity of butamirate citrate linctus versus clobutinol syrup. PubMed PMID: 2095610.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

common: Nausea and drowsiness were the main reported adverse effects in the short active-comparator trial; its size and duration cannot define uncommon risks [[BUTA-CLIN]].

renal: The cited studies do not establish a CKD adjustment or dialysis schedule. A cough-challenge result is not renal safety evidence [[BUTA-CHALLENGE,BUTA-CLIN]].
